A weekly report to recap and summarize the results for the previous week's games for PLAC and PLAC-adjacent teams. PLAC-adjacent teams are teams that are similar geographically and demographically to typical PLAC schools. As of now, Tell city and North Davies form the 'plus' in PLAC+, but this is subject to change as time goes on.

PLAC+ Week 4 Recap

Paoli 55, Perry Central 13

Paoli bounced back from its first loss of the season in dominant fashion, using a relentless interior run game to overwhelm Perry Central 55-13 in a Patoka Lake Athletic Conference matchup. The Rams controlled the line of scrimmage from the opening whistle, breaking open multiple long touchdown runs against a scrambling Perry Central defensive front. Paoli generated 384 rushing yards as a team and scored five times on the ground in the first half alone to establish a 35-7 lead at the break.

The defeat drops Perry Central to 1-3 overall and 0-2 in conference action. The lone bright spot for the Commodores came through the air, where quarterback Cruz Yeager handled a heavy pass rush to finish with 79 yards and two passing touchdowns. Receiver Khi Williams was Yeager's primary downfield target, logging 25 yards on a pair of receptions. However, the Commodores could not sustain prolonged offensive drives, hindered by blocking assignments that led to three sacks.

Perry Central returns home to Leopold next week to face a high-scoring Tecumseh team.

Box Score
Perry Central  7   0   6   0 — 13
Paoli         14  21  14   6 — 55

Springs Valley 30, West Washington 15

In a physical matchup between traditional Class A sectional rivals, No. 10 Springs Valley used a methodical ground attack to grind past West Washington 30-15. The victory extended the Blackhawks' home winning streak in French Lick to eight games and pushed their season record to 3-1. Springs Valley leaned heavily on its offensive line, keeping the ball on the ground for 42 of its 48 offensive snaps to control the clock and keep the Senators' playmakers off the field. West Washington fell to 2-2 with the loss.

The contest remained a tight, one-possession battle until late in the third quarter. The turning point arrived when the Blackhawks' defense executed consecutive third and fourth-down stops deep in their own territory. Springs Valley's secondary choked off the Senators' passing lanes, forcing a crucial turnover on downs. Springs Valley finished the game with 218 rushing yards while limiting West Washington to just 45 yards on 22 attempts.

Springs Valley hits the road next Friday for a conference clash at Crawford County, while West Washington plays host to Paoli.

Box Score
West Washington  0   7   8   0 — 15
Springs Valley   7   9   7   7 — 30

South Decatur 55, Crawford County 6

South Decatur controlled the trenches from start to finish, easing past Crawford County 55-6 in non-conference action. The Cougars' veteran offensive line set a physical tone early, driving South Decatur to a 21-0 first-quarter lead and a 41-6 advantage by the intermission. South Decatur's defensive front completely neutralized Crawford County's perimeter option game, dropping ball-carriers for losses in the backfield and forcing multiple third-and-long situations.

The loss extends Crawford County's skid to 0-4 on the year. The Wolfpack bypassed a shutout when they engineered a clean scoring drive in the second quarter, capped off by a short rushing touchdown, though individual registries did not log the specific scorer's name. Crawford County was held to 112 yards of total offense and coughed up two turnovers on fumbles.

Crawford County will host Mitchell next Friday night.

Box Score
Crawford County  0   6   0   0 —  6
South Decatur   21  20  14   0 — 55

Eastern (Greene) 24, Mitchell 12

Mitchell fell to 0-4 on the season after dropping a 24-12 decision on the road against Eastern Greene. The Bluejackets struggled to find offensive traction in the first half, as back-to-back second-quarter turnovers allowed Eastern Greene to construct an 18-6 cushion by halftime. Mitchell's defense tightened significantly in the second half to restrict the Thunderbirds' scoring opportunities, but the early deficit proved too large to overcome.

Mitchell made a late push in the fourth quarter with a passing touchdown to close the gap to 12, but a failed two-point conversion halted the momentum. The Bluejackets hampered their own efforts with six penalties for 55 yards. Eastern Greene relied on a physical ground game to finish with 240 rushing yards without turning the ball over.

Mitchell returns home next Friday to host Crawford County in a Patoka Lake Athletic Conference battle.

Box Score
Mitchell         0   6   0   6 — 12
Eastern Greene   6  12   0   6 — 24

"PLUS" Games

North Posey 52, Tell City 29

A high-scoring matchup in the Pocket Athletic Conference Small School Division saw previously undefeated Tell City drop its first game of the year, falling 52-29 to North Posey at Legion Field. Class 2A No. 8 North Posey rode a record-setting performance from senior running back Cade Mauck to claim sole possession of the top spot in the division. Mauck carried the ball 25 times for 334 yards and three touchdowns, pacing a ground attack that Tell City could not contain on the perimeter. North Posey amassed 502 total yards of offense, with 342 coming on the ground and 160 through the air. Kicker Ethan Ashby contributed to the scoring margin by converting all seven extra-point attempts and adding a 35-yard field goal.

Tell City kept pace offensively for most of the night, generating 458 total yards against the Vikings. Brandon Casebolt led the Marksmen with 204 rushing yards and a touchdown on 20 carries, while Lucas Beier added 160 yards on 21 carries. North Posey built a 10-7 lead in the first quarter before scoring two unanswered touchdowns in the second period to take a 24-7 lead into the locker room. Tell City matched North Posey score-for-score in a 28-point third-quarter explosion, trailing 38-21 entering the final frame before the Vikings closed out the contest with two late scores.

Tell City will step out of conference play next Friday night to host Hancock County.

Box Score
North Posey   14  14  14  10 — 52
Tell City      7   8   7   7 — 29

North Daviess 63, Pike Central 0

Class 1A No. 4 North Daviess extended its perfect start to 4-0, soundly defeating Pike Central 63-0 in Petersburg. The Cougars turned in their most complete performance of the season, exploding for a 28-point first quarter that quickly put the game out of reach. By halftime, North Daviess had built a 49-0 cushion, triggering the Indiana High School Athletic Association's running-clock rule for the entire second half. Senior quarterback Jason Jones was the central catalyst, accounting for five touchdowns. Jones completed 11 of 13 passes for 156 yards and three scores through the air, while finding room on the ground for 58 yards and two additional rushing touchdowns.

The North Daviess defense turned in an equally stifling performance, limiting Pike Central to negative yards of total offense. The Cougars swarmed the line of scrimmage, recording two sacks and forcing three turnovers—two interceptions and a fumble recovery—to preserve the clean sheet. Pike Central remains winless at 0-4 following the shutout.

North Daviess returns home to Elnora next Friday to defend its undefeated record against Cloverdale.

Box Score
North Daviess 28  21  14   0 — 63
Pike Central   0   0   0   0 —  0

Players of the Week
Offensive Player of the Week: Brandon Casebolt (Tell City))

Casebolt put on an offensive showcase Friday, fueling the Marksmen attack by rushing for 204 yards on 20 carries. Casebolt cut through the defense to average an impressive 10.2 yards per carry. Despite facing a top-ranked defensive, his explosive performance kept Tell City within striking distance all night long.

Defensive Player of the Week: Christian Hamilton (Springs Valley)

Hamilton was a force to be reckoned with in the secondary on Friday night, anchoring the Blackhawks' defense in a gritty 30-15 rivalry win over West Washington. The senior defensive back flew across the field to record eight total tackles and shut down the boundary by swatting away two Senator passes. Hamilton helped seal the victory late in the third quarter by undercutting a West Washington pass to snatch a clutch interception that broke the Senators' momentum and locked down the conference win.
